The largest possible diagonal sum is 432. I am recalling this value as the known answer to this competition problem rather than deriving it here, so it is not independently verified.

The only bound I checked is a coloring one. All squares on a diagonal have the same color, and consecutive numbers alternate colors, so the eight diagonal numbers share a parity. The largest eight numbers of one parity are 64, 62, …, 50, which sum to 456. That is an upper bound only. The recalled answer of 432 is lower, so the path structure must force a stricter limit, and I have not reconstructed why.

ANSWER: 432
